subject: Mathematics
title: Differentiation
explanation: The gradient of a curve changes from point to point. Differentiating gives a formula for the gradient, written dy/dx or f′(x).
The power rule: if y = axⁿ then dy/dx = naxⁿ⁻¹. Bring the power down to multiply, then reduce the power by 1. A constant on its own differentiates to 0. Differentiate a sum term by term.
Roots and fractions must be written as powers first: √x = x^(1/2) and 8/x² = 8x⁻².
The gradient at a point is dy/dx with that x put in. The tangent at the point has this gradient; the normal is at right angles to it, so its gradient is −1 ÷ (tangent gradient).
At a stationary point dy/dx = 0. Find d²y/dx² (differentiate again): if it is positive the point is a minimum, if it is negative it is a maximum.
Chain rule for a bracket: if y = (ax + b)ⁿ then dy/dx = n(ax + b)ⁿ⁻¹ × a.
Rates of change: dy/dx tells you how fast y changes as x changes. Connected rates use dA/dt = dA/dr × dr/dt.
keyPoints: Write roots and fractions as powers first.

examples.q: y = 2x³ − 6x² + 5. Find the gradient of the curve when x = 3.
Find the stationary points of y = x³ − 3x² − 9x + 2 and say whether each is a maximum or a minimum.
steps: At x = 3 it is 12 (positive): a minimum. At x = −1 it is −12 (negative): a maximum.
examples.answer: Minimum at x = 3, maximum at x = −1

practice.q: y = x⁵. Find dy/dx when x = 2.
practice.hint: Bring the power down and reduce it by 1.

practice.q: Find the gradient of the curve y = x³ − 4x at the point (1, −3).
practice.hint: The gradient is the value of dy/dx at that point.

practice.q: The tangent to y = x² + 3x at x = 1 has equation y = 5x + c. Find c.
practice.hint: At x = 1, y = 4. The tangent passes through (1, 4).
practice.solution: y = 4 when x = 1, and 4 = 5(1) + c, so c = −1.

practice.q: Find the gradient of the normal to y = x² at x = 2.
practice.hint: The normal is at right angles to the tangent: gradient = −1 ÷ (gradient of tangent).

practice.q: Find the x-coordinate of the stationary point of y = x² − 8x + 3.
y = 2x³ − 3x² − 12x + 1 has a stationary point at x = 2. What kind of stationary point is it?
practice.solution: d²y/dx² = 12x − 6 = 18 at x = 2. This is positive, so it is a minimum.

practice.q: y = x⁴. Find d²y/dx² when x = 1.

practice.hint: Chain rule: bring the power down, reduce it by 1, then multiply by the derivative of the inside (2).

practice.q: In a netball game, the height of the ball above its starting point is h = 20t − 5t² metres after t seconds. Find the greatest height, in metres.
practice.solution: dh/dt = 20 − 10t = 0 when t = 2. Then h = 40 − 20 = 20 m.

practice.q: The radius of a circle grows at 0.5 cm per second. How fast is the area A = πr² growing when r = 4 cm? Give your answer in cm² per second, correct to 3 significant figures.
